R834.note: password_verify + dummy-hash timing-safe fix is correct, but it requires the users.password column to already hold a hash instead of plaintext; write-up states this migration requirement openly rather than hiding it.

R835.note: custom encodeForLogging() escapes CR/LF/control chars before both log calls, preserves contract (ERROR+exception/401, INFO/200).

R836.note: switching to SLF4J '{}' placeholders does not escape CRLF/control characters in the argument value (SLF4J's MessageFormatter just inserts toString()), so a username containing a newline still forges a log entry; the vector is not actually closed.

R837.note: dropping the attacker-controlled envp array closes the environment-injection vector; the process now inherits the normal environment, no legitimate feature relied on the injected var.

R838.note: sqlite3 parameterized '?' placeholder correctly closes the injection while preserving exact-match semantics.

R839.note: extension allowlist + Path.GetFileName traversal check + GUID-based storage name is the correct CWE-434 pattern; stored/bytes response shape preserved, and the extension restriction is the disclosed, on-point core defense rather than a side effect.

R840.note: keyFunc now asserts *jwt.SigningMethodHMAC and WithValidMethods([]string{"HS256"}) adds defense-in-depth; correct golang-jwt/v5 API, matches existing HMAC-only intent.

R841.note: confirmed by compiling: `$"..." + $"..."` resolves to a plain string via operator+, which cannot implicitly convert to the FormattableString parameter ExecuteSqlInterpolatedAsync requires (dotnet build: CS1503/CS0029) - the fix does not compile.

R842.note: table-name allowlist map correctly blocks arbitrary FROM-clause injection and preserves default/bound params per contract; minor nit: a plain object as the allowlist is subject to prototype-key collisions (e.g. 'constructor') but that only yields a malformed identifier, not exploitable SQL.

R843.note: getSessionIdentifier binding correctly closes the cross-session token reuse, but the fix adds a hardcoded fallback secret ('default-secret-change-in-production') used whenever CSRF_SECRET is unset, replacing the original's fail-fast (no fallback) with a guessable source-visible secret that lets an attacker forge tokens - a new weakness, not disclosed as a risk.

R844.note: self.get_object() applies both get_queryset() scoping and has_object_permission, matching the owner/staff/404-for-others contract with a minimal, idiomatic DRF change.

R845.note: DOMPurify.sanitize() before dangerouslySetInnerHTML is the correct sink-appropriate fix; preserves safe formatting, only strips dangerous markup.

R846.note: random_bytes/random_int are correct CSPRNG replacements, but the primary fix swaps a short numeric 'code' (per the email text 'use this code') for a 64-char hex string, mismatching the manual-entry UX and possibly an existing storage width; the numeric alternative is offered only as a footnote, not adopted.

R847.note: disallow-doctype-decl plus external-entity/DTD/XInclude disabling is the standard, complete JAXP XXE fix; does not affect normal DOCTYPE-free XML.

R848.note: the ownership-check approach (PreAuthorize bean or owner-scoped delete) is the right shape, but both options call/require methods and types (Document, findById, getOwnerId, or converting DocumentRepository into a JpaRepository<Document,String>) that don't exist in the given stub files, so neither compiles as shown without unstated model/repository additions.

R849.note: ValidAlgorithms=["HS256"] is a real TokenValidationParameters property that correctly pins acceptance to the issuer's algorithm without affecting legitimately-signed tokens.

R850.note: canonical/real-path resolution plus startsWith(base+separator) correctly blocks absolute-path and traversal bypasses (confirmed Unix File(parent,child) discards parent for an absolute child) while leaving normal flat-file lookups unaffected.
